html:
The part of the Roman Empire ruled by the emperor Galerius under the Tetrarchy: the Balkans and Greece. The map shows it in 300.

Galerius was a soldier from the Danube lands whom Diocletian made junior emperor in 293, alongside Constantius in the west. He fought on the Danube and in the east, and in 298 won a great victory over the Persian king Narseh that gained Rome land beyond the Tigris from the Sasanian Empire. He made Thessalonica his capital; his triumphal arch and the round building now called the Rotunda still stand there.

Galerius was the strongest voice behind the Great Persecution of Christians that began in 303, and he became senior emperor in 305. Dying of a painful illness in 311, he issued an edict at Serdica that ended the persecution and let Christians worship. Two years later Constantine and Licinius went further. The neighbouring share in Italy and Africa was Maximian's.
sum: The part of the Roman Empire ruled by the emperor Galerius under the Tetrarchy: the Balkans and Greece. The map shows it in 300.
